statement: The explicit rational triple in Theorem 4.3 is strongly general and has 184 distinct geometric tangent circles: exactly 160 real circles with positive squared radius and 24 nonreal circles forming 12 conjugate pairs. The same real count occurs on a nonempty Euclidean open set of strongly general real triples.

source.location: Theorems 1.1, 4.2 and 4.3; Section 6.1, fixed rational fibre delta_0=1/500000 (attainability consequence)

scope: Attainability for the explicit smooth conic triple over Q in Theorem 4.3, with delta_0=1/500000, and on a nonempty Euclidean open set of strongly general real triples. The tangent-circle scheme is finite and étale, all solution circles are smooth, and contacts are ordinary with transverse residual intersections. Exactly 160 real circles have positive squared radius; the remaining 24 geometric circles are nonreal.
notes: An individual attainable count; this does not settle the complete spectrum.
